newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank plans unchanged dividend for '96.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank plans unchanged dividend for '96.

text.p: Commerzbank AG, Germany's third-largest commercial bank, said on Tuesday it planned to pay an unchanged dividend of 1.35 marks per five-mark share for 1996 and that its net profit rose 22 percent to approximately 1.19 billion marks.

The bank said it was increasing its reserves by 650 million marks from 1996 earnings, up from a transfer of 400 million marks made from its 1995 profits. The total dividend payout for 1996 is 540 million marks.
The unchanged dividend was expected but the net profit was below analysts' expectations for a figure of about 1.3 billion marks.
Commerzbank released the 1996 allocation to reserves and dividend payout in a mandatory statement.

A spokesman for the bank said in response to a Reuter enquiry that the net profit "roughly" amounted to the sum total of the dividend payout and the allocation to reserves, although the figure was not exact as it it did not contain two smaller items.
Commerzbank also said it had a "good start" in 1997 due in part to favourable capital market conditions.
The bank's group balance sheet total rose by 11.5 percent to 451 billion marks by the end of 1996, driven by a 20 percent jump in lending to 312 billion marks.
The lending rise was caused by increases in lending to local authorities and to banks, Commerzbank said.
